### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`  _(via handleRequest (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via handleRequest (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 295ce127e0ff5167def12353ddf37c9ca31f74e0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3e67de58753aadf0120fb46576bf91eaf1a618f4` — the merge of head `c8abb2726467e0fdb378f4035273e641fbf03fb3` into base `295ce127e0ff5167def12353ddf37c9ca31f74e0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3e67de58753aadf0120fb46576bf91eaf1a618f4 && git checkout 3e67de58753aadf0120fb46576bf91eaf1a618f4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 295ce127e0ff5167def12353ddf37c9ca31f74e0 c8abb2726467e0fdb378f4035273e641fbf03fb3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 295ce127e0ff5167def12353ddf37c9ca31f74e0 && git merge --no-ff c8abb2726467e0fdb378f4035273e641fbf03fb3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 295ce127e0ff5167def12353ddf37c9ca31f74e0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 295ce127e0ff5167def12353ddf37c9ca31f74e0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c8abb2726467e0fdb378f4035273e641fbf03fb3`
Local-runs: none
Scope: none (no reviewFace hits; the face is the needs:contract-review label alone) + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-request-routing.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/scim-bearer-cookie-origin.test.ts

Inputs read: card #33237 body and all five comments (triage 6875420457, claim 6877865244, downstream note 6878485932, dev report 6878554536, seat note 6878588507), the PR body, file list and net diff at this head, and the check-runs on this head. Live-tree code was read on `origin/main` at `d4fbb4dbb6`. The vendor packages (better-auth and `@better-auth/scim`) are not installed in the read-only tree, so statements about vendor behaviour rest on the in-tree pins and the green check-runs.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set, widened, right.** `handleRequest` now serves a `/scim/v2/*` request that carries a bearer and a Cookie with no Origin, where it was refused 403 before. This is the card's Expected and its first acceptance line, pinned by cases 1 and 2 of the new test, green on this head.
- **Accept-set, widened beyond the card's three cases, right.** A `/scim/v2/*` bearer request carrying a Cookie and an Origin the deployment does not trust now also reaches the SCIM bearer check. The card's Expected says a bearer-authenticated SCIM request is not subject to the browser origin/CSRF check, so this is inside the contract, and the dev disclosed it. The rebuilt request carries no cookie, so it has no more authority than the same request sent without one. No test pins this arm (nit 2).
- **Accept-set, unchanged, right.** A `/scim/v2/*` request with a Cookie and no bearer keeps its Cookie and is still refused (case 3). A cookie-authenticated non-SCIM POST with no Origin is still refused (case 4, the positive control). Paths outside `/scim/v2` are untouched: the predicate is `isScimProtocolPath`, the one the SCIM request scope already keys on.
- **Fail direction, right.** Where the predicate and the vendor router could disagree on a path spelling, the predicate answers "not SCIM", the Cookie stays and the previous refusal stands; where the bearer test matches but the vendor reads no SCIM credential, the vendor's own 401 answers (pinned on main by `scim-refusal-audit.test.ts`).
- **Mount layer, read, unchanged.** The one-account-per-request step hands on a request whose bearer names no session, so the fix takes effect in a deployment too; the other mount steps do not read the Cookie.
- **Public surface, none moved.** No export, schema, route or error code added or removed; `skipOriginCheck`, `disableCSRFCheck`, the trusted-origins list and the better-auth pin are untouched.
- **Check-runs.** Every gate-carrying lane on this head concluded success (Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, both type-check lanes, all lint lanes, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate).

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/33237-scim-bearer-cookie-origin.md` declares `@objectstack/plugin-auth` patch, matching a defect fix that admits requests the contract already meant to admit, with no API or schema change. `Clause-②: no` on the PR body, changeset and claim is right: no published schema or governed path, and no narrowing. Check Changeset is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` is empty and `security_findings` is `none`; agreed on both — the change removes an ambient credential from one request class and grants none.
- Out-of-scope note 1 (the vendor skips its origin check under a test NODE_ENV): answered; the harness sets the production value and asserts it, and cases 3 and 4 being green shows the check is live. No card needed.
- Out-of-scope note 2 (the untrusted-Origin arm): answered in ① as inside the card's Expected.
- Out-of-scope note 3 (the cloud proxy strip can retire): cloud's call on cloud#4491, not this PR's.
- File surface held: the claim's forbidden files are not in the diff.
- Docs Drift Check named two pages through `handleRequest`; neither states anything about the origin check on SCIM, so nothing there is made false.

### ④ Design judgment

**`auth-manager-request-routing.ts`, `handleRequest`: holds.** The strip runs after the client address is established and before the dev-only Origin synthesis and the vendor call; nothing later reads the Cookie on a SCIM path, and the refusal-audit arm still reads `authorization` from the rebuilt request. The comment's claims check out against the tree (the verifier reads only the token; writes are attributed to the verified connection; a no-bearer SCIM request is refused anyway), except the wording in nit 1. Four attempts to break it (path spelling divergence, authorization-value divergence, a session cookie beside a bearer, the one-account rule at the mount and in the before-hook) all leave the rebuilt request with no more authority than one sent with no Cookie.

**`scim-bearer-cookie-origin.test.ts`: holds.** The four cases map onto the card's three acceptance lines (POST and PATCH separate), and the harness defeats both ways the cases could pass vacuously.

Findings:
- **nit 1** (`auth-manager-request-routing.ts`, the new comment): "Dropping the Cookie relaxes no check" reads stricter than the code: for a bearer-carrying SCIM request the origin check no longer applies at all, which is the card's Expected. Accepted deviation or follow-up, since a fix moves the head.
- **nit 2** (`scim-bearer-cookie-origin.test.ts`): the untrusted-Origin arm has no pinning case; a follow-up case would keep it from regressing unnoticed.
- **nit 3** (`scim-bearer-cookie-origin.test.ts`): the harness drives a manager with no bound route table, so the mount middlewares are not on the path; read and found to hand the request on. Coverage only.

No must-fix and no should-fix.

Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5nhu4dRbKVQKDB4CDB`

**VERDICT: PASS**
